answer: A new identity earns almost nothing at first. Its payout cap rises only after months of graded work, so full earnings take patience no farm can fake cheaply. A sybil operator wants an ocean of accounts paying out on day one, yet each account here crawls through the same slow ramp, and keeping ten thousand identities graded and consistent for six months costs more than they will ever withdraw. When graders spot shared fingerprints, a whisper moves down the review queue and the registry stains the whole cluster umber, a brown mark any buyer can check before paying.
